sources.citation: OLAC. 2025. Resources in and about the Trimuris language (combined catalog, up-to-date 2025-11-04; Internet Archive copy 2025-11-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary item in the world's archives is 'Bagusa Trimurus Wordlist DeVries. DeVries, Jim (researcher). 1985. SIL International. oai:sil.org:68569' (Lexical resources). 'Language descriptions' = Glottolog entry only. No grammar, sketch, or phonology exists in OLAC.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2017. A grammar of Papuan Malay. (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 11.) Berlin: Language Science Press. sec. 1.4 p.13; Appendix C p.682.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.13: 'For the remaining eight languages no resources are available except for their listing in the Ethnologue (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2016a) and Glottolog (Nordhoff et al. 2013): Bagusa, Betaf, Jofotek-Bromnya, Keijar, Kwerba Mamberamo, Kwinsu, Trimuris, and Wares.' Appendix C row 'Trimuris [tip]' has no survey/lexicon/grammar/literacy ticks.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Trimuris' / 'Nopuk' / 'Nupuk' do not occur anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent). Trimuris is not distinguished from Kwerba (no. 68). Wordlist key p.92: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. New Guinea World: Kwerba (Northwest New Guinea > Foja Range > West Foja Range > Apauwar River). Santa Fe Institute. (Internet Archive copy 2022-10-06; live site now login-walled.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Page 'under construction', no data. Its Kwerba-family source list is the fullest bibliography seen; the only Trimuris item is 'Donohue (2005: 427-428) reflexes of proto-Kwerba /*s/ with eight terms from Anggreso, Kwerba, Kasonaweja, Trimuris and Bagusa villages'. Also lists 'de Vries (1991) Kwerba (unobtained)' and 'Kim (1999) phonology of Kwerba of Aurimi village (unobtained)'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd ed., entry 'Trimuris'. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Pop. 300 (1999 SIL); Jayapura regency, Mamberamo Tengah, Mamberamo east bank; classification Tor-Kwerba > Greater Kwerba > Kwerba > Nuclear; 'Dialects: None known. Low intelligibility of Kwerba [kwe]. Lexical similarity: 70% with Kauwera [xau] and 60% with Kwerba [kwe].' Language resources: OLAC only.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. 18 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Trimuris appears only on the survey map (p.4) and as a leaf of the Kwerba-subfamily tree ('Bagusa Kwerba-Aurimi Trimuris Kauwera Kwerba-Mam.', p.10). Phonology notes (sec. 4.3) cover Airoran and Samarokena only. Nothing on Trimuris. References cite DeVries 1991 'Kwerba' ms and Kim 1999 'Kwerba phonology' ms (SIL Abepura).

sources.citation: De Vries, James A. & Sandra A. De Vries. 1997. An overview of Kwerba verb morphology. In A. Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 3, 1-35. Pacific Linguistics A-87.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Kwerba of Aurimi only. p.1: 'Closely related languages include Nopuk, Bagusa, Kauwerawec, and Airoran (Silzer and Clouse 1991:25).' No phonology section; nothing on Trimuris/Nopuk stress.

sources.citation: DeVries, Jim. 1991. Kwerba. UNCEN-SIL ms. Abepura: Summer Institute of Linguistics.

sources.note: Unpublished Kwerba sketch by the same SIL researcher who took the 1985 Trimuris wordlist; may include comparative notes on the Nupuk/Trimuris variety and on Kwerba stress. Cited by Clouse, Donohue & Ma 2002; 'unobtained' for Usher.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: A comprehensive guide, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Family-level survey covering the Kwerba (Foja Range) languages; would report any known Kwerba-family stress generalisation and confirm the absence of Trimuris material. Paywalled chapter.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2005. Syntactic and lexical factors conditioning the diffusion of sound change. Oceanic Linguistics 44(2): 427-442.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Only peer-reviewed publication with Trimuris data (eight terms from 'Trimuris village' in a proto-Kwerba *s-reflex table, pp. 427-428, per Usher); Donohue's own Kwerba-family field data may carry a transcription/stress remark applying to all the varieties compared.

sources.citation: Kim, Yon-Soo. 1999. Kwerba phonology. Unpublished ms. Abepura: Summer Institute of Linguistics (UNCEN-SIL).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Nearest-relative phonology (Kwerba of Aurimi; Trimuris has 60% lexical similarity with Kwerba and 'low intelligibility'). Would give the Kwerba-family stress pattern that a Trimuris description would most likely share; cited by Clouse, Donohue & Ma 2002 and Usher ('unobtained').

sources.citation: DeVries, Jim. 1985. Bagusa Trimurus Wordlist (Nupuk of kampung Trimuris). 5 pp., 208 entries, transcribed on paper 1985-12-27. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 68569, Dallas: SIL International.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: no other copy located; the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: The only primary-language document for Trimuris in existence (OLAC's sole lexical resource; Glottolog ref 570520). Hand transcription may carry stress/accent marks or a transcription note; it is the only place a first-hand observation of Trimuris prosody could be. Lands online; needs a browser/human to pass the an automated-access block.

sources.citation: van der Leeden, Alexander Cornelis. 1954. Verslag over taalgebieden in het Sarmische van de Ambtenaar van het Kantoor voor Bevolkingszaken. 15 pp. Hollandia: Gouvernement van Nederlands-Nieuw-Guinea, Dienst van Binnenlandse Zaken, Kantoor voor Bevolkingszaken (vol. 35).

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest report to name a Trimuris language area (Glottolog ref 29762, 15 languages incl. Trimuris); a Dutch administrative language-area survey, so a stress note is unlikely, but it is the only other item Glottolog links to trim1239.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference records 570520 (DeVries 1985 'Nupuk (Bagusa)', 5 pp wordlist, language code Trimuris 'Nupuk of kampung Trimurus'), 29762 (van der Leeden 1954, 15 pp Dutch admin report on Sarmi language areas), 548534 (Du Buy 1955, Adatrechtbundels 45: 102-107, 'Masiwa-Trimoeris'), 65901 (Donohue 2005); Glottolog languoid trim1239 (0 descriptive refs); Wikipedia en/sw; Wikidata Q7842270; iso639-3.sil.org/code/tip
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Bibliographic only. All four Glottolog refs are overview/wordlist types (listed by Glottolog as an overview x3, wordlist x1); none is a grammar, sketch or phonology. No stress information anywhere.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 68569: DeVries, Jim. 1985 (1985-12-27). Bagusa Trimurus Wordlist. 5 pages, 208 entries; 'PDF of 5-page wordlist transcribed on paper in 1985. GIF images included'; Draft; subject language Trimuris [tip]; content language Indonesian.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Record page. the PDF (1.06 MB) and GIF zip are behind an automated-access block by automated download (not reachable by automated download 'Just a moment..'), not in the Internet Archive, Save-Page-Now returned 500. Content unread. A hand-transcribed 208-item survey wordlist with Indonesian glosses; may carry stress marks but no prose statement is expected.

sources.note: No scan of any primary source for Trimuris exists on archive.org; the discovery services that could not be queried are recorded so a later reading with web search can retry, but Kluge 2017, OLAC and Usher's bibliography agree that nothing beyond the 1985 wordlist and Donohue's eight forms exists.
